summary: Map a signed dimensionless grid to p_n = x*vnorm/clight; vnorm and clight must be velocities in the same unit, and a dimensionless thermal speed ratio must not be passed directly. Intermediate overflow and final non-representability are handled separately, so a representable result is neither falsely rejected nor lost to intermediate underflow.

capability: Map a signed dimensionless grid to p_n = x*vnorm/clight without automatic unit conversion.
operation: Map a signed dimensionless grid to normalized momentum
discovery.model: Independent closed-form definition, not a fit; dangerous intermediates are evaluated at high precision beyond binary64, with no automatic unit conversion.
discovery.geometry: Not applicable; an elementwise scaling of a caller-supplied one-dimensional dimensionless grid, not a spatial coordinate.
discovery.boundary: A zero velocity scale returns signed zero and the map is odd in x; intermediate overflow does not cause false rejection; a genuinely tiny final value may round to signed zero, while final overflow is rejected.

identity.relation: the normalized momentum profile p_n on a grid, from the grid, a velocity scale and the speed of light
identity.definition: Returns the dimensionless p_n = x*vnorm/clight elementwise; vnorm and clight must be velocities in the same unit. The ordinary region retains the original binary64 evaluation order; when an intermediate value overflows or becomes subnormal, the exact input floats are evaluated with 100-digit Decimal and the final result is rounded to binary64.
identity.model: an independent closed-form definition, not a fit; beyond ordinary binary64 arithmetic, dangerous intermediates are evaluated at high precision, with no automatic unit conversion
identity.geometry: not applicable; an elementwise scaling of a one-dimensional grid
identity.coordinates: not applicable; the grid is a caller-supplied dimensionless coordinate, not a spatial coordinate
identity.boundary: a zero velocity scale gives signed zero, and the map is odd in x; intermediate product overflow does not cause false rejection. A genuinely tiny final value may round to signed zero in binary64, while final overflow is still rejected
assumptions: x is a signed dimensionless one-dimensional grid; vnorm >= 0, clight > 0, and both velocities use the same unit. The implementation cannot verify units automatically.

the two leaf entries are independent. A thermal speed ratio must not be passed as vnorm; the direct composition divides by c twice, so the caller must first multiply it by the speed of light to recover a velocity.
the ordinary region retains the original floating-point operation order; bit-for-bit agreement with the erroneous earlier operation at dangerous extremes is not promised.
shapes and finite inputs are checked first; the existing float() behavior for convertible non-real values is preserved, without adding physical meaning.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: The grid the map is evaluated on, dimensionless and signed.
inputs.constraints: A finite one-dimensional array; it is converted with numpy.asarray and is not modified in place. A negative entry is accepted.

inputs.name: vnorm
inputs.description: The velocity scale the grid is scaled by, in the same unit as clight.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative, and scalar-shaped: a list, a tuple or an array with one or more dimensions is rejected by parameter name rather than converted. A dimensionless speed ratio is not a velocity and is not a valid value here.

inputs.name: clight
inputs.description: The speed of light in the unit the caller is working in; 2.99792458e10 for cm/s.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive, and scalar-shaped. The value is the caller's: this asset states no speed of light of its own and performs no unit conversion.

outputs.name: p_n
outputs.description: The normalized momentum profile x * vnorm / clight, dimensionless, with the grid's shape.
outputs.constraints: a float64 array with the same shape as x; signed and finally finite, while a genuinely tiny value may round to zero under floating-point rules. Intermediate floating-point overflow must not be misread as final closed-form non-representability

preconditions: The caller has a grid of dimensionless momenta coordinates and a velocity scale for the species.
vnorm and clight are already expressed in the same velocity unit.
supported: ordinary inputs retain the original scientific relation and double-precision operation order
dangerous intermediates use a Decimal fallback evaluated from the exact input floats; the input domain is not narrowed and verification tolerances are not relaxed
inputs with an invalid shape or a violated finiteness or sign contract are rejected by parameter name; final overflow is rejected and no partial result is returned
excluded: Composition with scirel.collisions.thermal-electron-momentum: the two leaves are dimensionally incompatible and the direct composition divides by c twice, so it is not provided. A caller that wants the dimensionless grid momentum x * p_Te must convert the ratio to a velocity first, for example vnorm = p_Te * clight, and that conversion is the caller's step.
Any unit conversion between vnorm and clight; the relation assumes a common unit and cannot verify it.
Any statement of the speed of light or of any other physical constant; every constant is the caller's.
Any requirement that the momentum be nonnegative, which belongs to the electron-ion leaf.
The four Coulomb-log mappings of the same family: they are different relations and are not published with these two leaves.
a final result outside the binary64 representable range is rejected; an overflowing intermediate result is not itself excluded

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when x is not a finite one-dimensional array, when vnorm or clight is not scalar-shaped, or when vnorm is negative or non-finite or clight is non-positive or non-finite, with a message naming the offending parameter.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: raises ValueError only when the final value is still non-finite after the fallback computation. Intermediate product or quotient overflow, underflow or subnormal precision loss triggers the high-precision fallback rather than directly rejecting the input.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this operator has no iteration or feedback.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no profile.

example.description: demonstrate the retained ordinary relation together with the final result after correcting extreme intermediates
example.code:
from scirel.collisions import normalized_momentum
import numpy as np
p = normalized_momentum(x=[-1e308,0.,1e308],vnorm=1e308,clight=1e308)
assert np.array_equal(p,[-1e308,0.,1e308])
small = normalized_momentum(x=[1e-300],vnorm=1e-100,clight=1e-200)
assert small[0] > 0
print(p,small)
example.expected: returns [-1e308, 0, 1e308] and approximately [1.0000000000000001e-200]; intermediate product overflow or underflow does not lose a final representable result
